findings.title: Claims F21 is not fixed: the page's new explanation for the 26 vs 27 gap is wrong, and the example is not 'the same shape'
findings.evidence:
The page now says: "The example is the median soldier at 1.80 m ... The limits section reads the same shape at 27 from a larger drawing; the reading moves by a few percent with the drawing's size." exampleSheet() still draws e.girths, his own girths at 1.755 m, on a 1.80 m frame. compute_limits.js uses calc.compute({heightM: 1.8}), his shape scaled to 1.80 m. Script scratchpad/review2/s/f21.js, page settings (1,060 kg/m³, 7.5% fat):
- page example, own girths, 700 px, default refine: 25.70 (90.0 kg)
- own girths at 800 px: 25.82
- own girths at 1,600 px: 25.82
- girths at 1.80 m, 800 px: 27.26, which is limits.json score_at_f1
A larger drawing changes the reading by 0.5%. The girth basis changes it by (1.8/1.755)² = 5.2%. The round 1 verifier gave this cause and fix (round1.json, claims F21 better_fix). HEAD kept the explanation the verifier had shown to be wrong. round1.md says all 23 confirmed claims findings were fixed.
findings.expected: The tool example and the limits card read one stated shape and give one number. Otherwise the page gives the true cause of the difference.
findings.fix: In exampleSheet(), take girths at 1.80 m as drawTarget does: var r0 = calc.compute({ buildId: 'ansur2_m_p50', heightM: 1.8 }); BuildCalc.SITES.forEach(function (s) { g[s] = r0.girths[s].value; }). Then delete the sentence 'The limits section reads the same shape at ... with the drawing's size.' The example then measures about 27, the same as the card.

findings.title: UX L8 is only half fixed: tapping the 924 ring at its centre or anywhere on its left half still jumps to 'Empty to the end'
findings.location: build-comparison/src/app.html:1218 stopAt (now d <= best.d) and :1727 tapeJump; research/reviews/round1.md:83
findings.evidence: Script scratchpad/review2/s/l8.js taps the circle.m924 ring at offsets from its centre and records the id that jump() scrolls to. At 1280 px and 390 px (touch), on both the glance tape (ring 14 px) and the locator (ring 7 px): -6, -4, -2, -1 and 0 px go to 'empty-3'; +1 to +4 px go to 'meatball'. The round 1 verifier predicted this (round1.json L8): 'Changing to d <= best.d alone does not fix it: a tap a hair left of the ring centre still has gap d=0 and meatball d>0.' Its fix, a snap in tapeJump, was not applied. round1.md:83 says 'L8: the 924 ring jumps to the meatball.'
findings.expected: A tap anywhere on the ring, which marks the meatball, jumps to the meatball stop.
findings.fix: In tapeJump, before stopAt: if (Math.abs(x - X(MEAT)) <= 8) { jump('meatball'); return; }. Here x is the tap position in the host and X = host._X. Add the dx = -3 tap to shots.js.

findings.title: UX L1 is partly fixed: on the pressed segmented buttons the inside focus ring is 2.3:1 (light) and 1.7:1 (dark) against the button
findings.evidence:
Script scratchpad/review2/s/focus3.js focuses each segmented button with focusVisible. The ring now sits inside the button, so the button's fill is on both sides of it.
- Light, pressed hSame/vFront/zAll: ring rgb(31,79,166) on rgb(21,24,31), contrast 2.31:1
- Dark, pressed: ring rgb(148,181,255) on rgb(232,233,238), contrast 1.68:1. Screenshot scratchpad/review2/shots/f-hSame-dark.png shows a faint pale-blue ring.
The unpressed buttons are fine (7.3 and 8.3:1). The pressed buttons are the defaults (Same height, Front, Whole scale), so a keyboard user meets these first. The round 1 verifier's fix included 'a sheet-coloured inner ring so it also shows on the pressed (ink) button'. That part was not applied, and round1.md does not say so.
findings.expected: A focus indicator of at least 3:1 against the colours next to it (WCAG 1.4.11) on every segmented button, pressed or not.
findings.fix: Add: .seg button[aria-pressed="true"]:focus-visible { outline-color: var(--sheet); }. The sheet colour on the pressed fill gives 16.7:1 (light) and 13.9:1 (dark). Alternatively use the verifier's box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 4px var(--sheet).

findings.title: Claims F6 is partly fixed: the key still defines ESTIMATE as 'body fat assumed', but Brian Shaw's ESTIMATE rests on a reported body fat
findings.location: build-comparison/src/app.html:1698 (key: 'ESTIMATE: body fat assumed. DERIVED: body fat measured.') and :439 (forest sub: 'Every range is an estimate (body fat assumed) unless ...')
findings.evidence: scoreStatus now returns 'estimate' unless bodyFat.status is 'measured', so Brian Shaw's plate and forest row read ESTIMATE. His drawer shows 'BODY FAT 18% (15–21%) REPORTED The build's own measured or reported value' (scratchpad/review2/drawers.json). He is the only build with bodyFat.status 'reported' (node check over model.all()). The key and the forest sub explain his chip as 'body fat assumed', which his own drawer contradicts. The round 1 verifier's better_fix was to reword both texts to 'ESTIMATE: body fat assumed or only reported'. They were not changed.
findings.expected: The key's meaning for each chip matches every build that carries it.
findings.fix: Key: 'ESTIMATE: body fat assumed or only reported. DERIVED: body fat measured in a study.' Forest sub: '... an estimate (body fat assumed or only reported) unless it carries a DERIVED chip (body fat measured)'.

findings.title: DC-14 is partly fixed: the DISPUTED chip still renders as a REPORTED chip, with the 'magazine, fan site' tooltip, in the key and in Sources
findings.location: build-comparison/src/app.html:1413 (Sources: chip(f.status === 'disputed' ? 'reported' : f.status, f.status)) and :1703 (key: chip(s === 'disputed' ? 'reported' : s, s))
findings.evidence: Script scratchpad/review2/s/dc14.js lists both chips whose text is 'disputed'. Each has class 'chip reported' and title 'Stated by a magazine, fan site, the athlete, or a secondary source; not independently measured.' One is the key's own row, next to the correct text 'Facts only (kept from the research): sources disagree.' The other is on 'Is the human mass-height exponent really about 2, or nearer 3?', whose sources are Med Hypotheses, Ann Hum Biol and AJCN. VOCAB already has a 'disputed' entry, so the remapping is not needed.
findings.expected: The DISPUTED chip's style and hover text say 'sources disagree', not the REPORTED definition.
findings.fix: Use chip('disputed') in both places, so the title comes from VOCAB.disputed and the class is 'chip disputed'. Add a .chip.disputed rule (for example, the reported style with a distinct border), so it does not look identical to REPORTED.

findings.title: Rex's tail: the page says 306 kg, while NOTES.md and builds.json say 307 kg; the round 1 verifier ruled 307 correct
findings.location: build-comparison/data/settings.json:514-515 (mass_kg 306, basis '0.289 m^3 ... 306 kg'), test/test.js:72-77; build-comparison/data/NOTES.md:43 ('Rex 307 kg'); build-calculator/data/builds.json rex tail (mass_kg_at_1060 307, 'about 307 kg'); research/reviews/round1.md:52
findings.evidence: The Rex drawer reads 'WEIGHT COUNTED 2,390 kg: 2,700 kg less 306 kg of tail ... tail 0.289 m^3 at 1,060 kg/m^3 ...: 306 kg'. NOTES.md:43 says 'Rex 307 kg (0.289 m³ at 1,060 kg/m³ ...)', and builds.json says 307. The verifier rejected F23 because 307 is the correct value: history/scratchpad/mass/checker/results_checker.json has tail 0.2894122456, and 0.28941 × 1,060 = 306.8, which rounds to 307. Its better_fix was to revert to 307. round1.md:52 says only 'was judged not a defect; the page uses 306', so the record hides that the change it kept was judged the less accurate one. The repo now gives two values for one quantity.
findings.expected: One tail mass everywhere, the one the unrounded measurement gives (307 kg).
findings.fix: Set settings.json rex exclude_mass mass_kg 307 with basis 'tail 0.2894 m^3 at 1,060 kg/m^3 ...: 307 kg', and test.js to 2700 − 307. Rebuild. Reword round1.md:52 to give the verdict (307 kept).

findings.title: round1.md overstates the per-view refinement speed-up ('about a third faster')
findings.evidence:
Scripts scratchpad/review2/s/prof.js and s/refine_browser.js compare measure.js at 3cd65f5 (whole-sheet refinement) with HEAD (refineViews). The input is the 2,000 px median-soldier sheet, 4,479 × 2,320 px, made with templateViews and renderSheet.
- Node, refinement only: 8,866 and 8,244 ms (old) against 7,091 and 7,115 ms (new), 14–20% faster
- Node, full measureSheet: 10,723 and 10,014 ms against 8,819 and 8,986 ms
- Chromium, full measureSheet: 11,481 and 10,737 ms against 9,611 and 10,698 ms (0–16%)
The masks are identical (0 pixels differ) and so is the score (26.95). The worker and 'about 10 s' parts of the row are true: 10.1 s in the page, with a largest timer gap of 171 ms while it runs.
findings.expected: The review record gives the speed-up it measured.
findings.fix: Change 'about a third faster' to 'about 10–20% faster (refinement 8.2–8.9 s down to 7.1 s on a 2,000 px sheet)'. Alternatively, make it faster, for example by refining only a band a few pixels wide around the coarse mask edge.

findings.title: round1.md says each archive.org API source now shows its quote and its book's page; 4 of 21 show neither, including the official 1987 handbook hit
findings.evidence: A Python check over data/facts.json found 21 page_production sources, 4 with no 'it matched' quote. All 4 are in asgardian_tissue_density_ohotmu ('OHOTMU 1987 TPB vol 4: same phrases'; 'times the density' AND Asgardian; 'dense/denser/density') and asgardian_tissue_density_dk. research/archive_snippets.json stores a hit for the 1987 handbook (officialhandbook04grue, an official item): '... bone is about 3 times {{{denser than similar human tissue}}}, contributing to the Asgardians ...'. QUOTE_PICK for this fact requires 'Asgardian flesh and bone|flesh and bone is about (three|3) times', and the highlight begins at 'and bone', so neither the quote nor the item page is added. The asgardian_tissue_density_dk search is stored as {'error': 'HTTP Error 400: Bad Request'}. DC-1 itself was rejected as a defect, so this concerns only the accuracy of the record.
findings.expected: The record's description of the hardening matches facts.json, or the 1987 handbook quote and its item link are added as described.
findings.fix: Widen QUOTE_PICK['asgardian_tissue_density_ohotmu'] to r'(flesh and )?bone is about (three|3) times|denser than similar human tissue', re-run tools/compile_facts.py and rebuild. Reword round1.md:58 to say which sources have no stored match.
